name: v1.0.2 — MIGRATION_CORE_V1
body:
HubSpot qualified end to end on one portal, all three halves reproducing, and a
correction to something this front got wrong.

## The portal was wrong, and that mattered

A HubSpot property export **carries no portal id anywhere in it** — the reader's
own design says so. The first export was recorded as coming from portal
`51872453` because that is where the credential of the day happened to point. It
was not. Every property it lists exists in portal `51050101` with none left over
— 209 contact, 115 company, 73 deal.

So the contract half was being built from **one portal's export and another
portal's supplement**, and nothing in either file would ever have said so.

The runner no longer carries the portal as a constant; it reads it from the
supplement the collector captured, because a constant is exactly what let the
runner describe one portal while the bundle described another. The evidence
records the attribution and how it was settled rather than quietly showing a
corrected number.

## Three halves, one portal, all reproducing

| half | evidence |
| --- | --- |
| target contract | 32 checks |
| import | 23 expectations, CRM Imports API |
| a property Kavo creates | 11 expectations |

The last of those is what `v1.0.0` said it could not show. The portal **enforces**
it rather than merely recording it: a second record carrying a key another record
already holds is refused, a value outside the enumeration Kavo defined is
refused, and an upsert keyed on the custom property matches — same record ids,
changed values, nothing duplicated.

## Which account this ran against

Portal `51050101` is a **standard** account holding the owner's real records,
supplied by them for this. The provenance says so, because anyone reading it
should know which kind of account the evidence came from. The qualification
removed everything it created — five records deleted, six properties archived,
both verified — and its cleanup matches on exact values rather than resemblance.

## Gates

| Gate | State |
| --- | --- |
| `CORE-CONSTITUTION-01`, `TARGET-CONTRACT-01` | PASS — 26 checks each |
| sabotage | PASS — 71/71 killed |
| `SF-TARGET-01`, `SF-OCR-01` | PASS — real org |
| `HSP-TARGET-01` | PASS — 32 + 23 + 11 expectations, one real portal |
| `FINAL-ADV-01` | PASS — 8 attacks |
| `CAPACITY-FOUNDING` | **MATERIAL_FAIL at 1,000,000** |

**Qualified for 500,000 source rows** at 3,971 MiB against a 5,734 MiB budget.
`MIGRATION_CORE_V1_FROZEN` = **FALSE**, derived from the gates rather than
declared. 1,146 tests, CI green on Ubuntu and Windows, Node 22 and 24.

name: v1.0.1 — MIGRATION_CORE_V1
body:
Two changes since `v1.0.0`: one claim withdrawn, one theory disproved.

## A property Kavo creates — settled

`v1.0.0` shipped saying it could not show whether a property **Kavo creates**
behaves like one HubSpot ships. Everything about unique-property matching had
been established on `email`, which HubSpot defines — evidence about HubSpot's
property rather than one of ours.

It is settled now, against a portal the account owner supplied for it, and the
portal **enforces** rather than merely records:

- a second record carrying a key another record already holds is **refused**;
- a value outside the enumeration Kavo defined is **refused**;
- an upsert keyed on the custom property matches — same record ids, changed
  values, nothing duplicated.

Eleven expectations, all met, on values the engine delivered. The account holds
the owner's real records, so the qualification removed what it created:
synthetic records deleted, six properties archived, both verified, with cleanup
matching on exact values rather than resemblance.

## The chunked decode — built, measured, reverted

The reader can be fed a file a piece at a time, and that is tested against the
whole-string reader over seventeen hostile inputs at every chunk size from one
character upward. What it does not do is lower the peak:

| how the verifier reads an artifact | 500,000 rows |
| --- | ---: |
| whole file, one decode | **3,971 MiB** |
| in 4 MiB pieces | 4,831 MiB |
| in 64 KiB pieces | 6,537 MiB, verification 5x slower |

A field is a slice of the text it was read from, and a slice keeps that text
alive. Reading whole means one parent per artifact. Reading in pieces means one
parent per piece, each pinned by whatever row was kept from it — and the smaller
the piece, the more parents a scattered set of retained values pins at once.

So the theory that peak memory was the whole-file decode is wrong. Three
attempts past the bounded point — a lineage projection and a chunked decode at
two sizes — all measured worse than doing nothing. The wiring is reverted; the
reader stays. The useful output is a direction: the **run** stage is 86% of the
budget before verification starts.

## Result

| Gate | State |
| --- | --- |
| `CORE-CONSTITUTION-01`, `TARGET-CONTRACT-01` | PASS |
| sabotage | PASS — 71/71 killed |
| `SF-TARGET-01`, `SF-OCR-01` | PASS — real org |
| `HSP-TARGET-01` | PASS — 32 + 23 + 11 expectations, two real portals |
| `FINAL-ADV-01` | PASS |
| `CAPACITY-FOUNDING` | **MATERIAL_FAIL at 1,000,000** |

**Qualified for 500,000 source rows.** `MIGRATION_CORE_V1_FROZEN` = **FALSE**,
derived from the gates rather than declared. 1,146 tests, CI green on Ubuntu and
Windows, Node 22 and 24.

name: v1.0.0 — MIGRATION_CORE_V1
body:
A deterministic, clean-room CRM migration engine. Reads a bundle of CSV and XLSX
files, decides what each source row becomes, and writes a package: the import
files for the destination plus the evidence for every decision. The same inputs
produce the same bytes.

`docs/release/MIGRATION_CORE_V1_PROVENANCE.md` and
`migration-core-v1-provenance.json` are the record. Both are generated from
tracked files and checked in CI, so a checkout can verify them rather than trust
them.

## `MIGRATION_CORE_V1_FROZEN` = FALSE

The flag is **derived from the gates, not asserted**. Seven are green; one is
not, so it reads false. Nobody can set it by hand while a gate is failing.

| Gate | State |
| --- | --- |
| `CORE-CONSTITUTION-01` | PASS — 26 checks |
| `TARGET-CONTRACT-01` | PASS — 26 checks |
| sabotage | PASS — 71 mutations, 71 killed, 0 survived |
| `SF-TARGET-01` | PASS — 11 contract checks + 23 Data Loader expectations, real org |
| `SF-OCR-01` | PASS — 8 expectations, real org |
| `HSP-TARGET-01` | PASS — 32 contract checks + 23 import expectations, real portal |
| `FINAL-ADV-01` | PASS — 8 attacks |
| `CAPACITY-FOUNDING` | **MATERIAL_FAIL at 1,000,000 rows** |

1,127 tests. CI green on Ubuntu and Windows, Node 22 and 24.

## What V1 is qualified for

**500,000 source rows, at 3,971 MiB against a 5,734 MiB budget.**

The 1,000,000 rung reaches 8,178 MiB and is recorded as failing rather than left
out. Correctness is exact at both: every row accounted for, the partition closed,
all 54 package checks passing with nothing reported. The failure is resource.

Where the budget goes at 1,000,000, from the harness's in-stage sampler:

| stage | peak | adds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| run | 4,950 MiB | — |
| package | 5,455 MiB | +505 |
| verify | 8,178 MiB | +2,723 |

The run stage alone is 86% of the budget before verification starts. Peak memory
here is **allocation volume**, not retention: each artifact is materialised as one
string, so verifying a 1,896 MB package decodes 1,896 MB of text. Removing the
retention of a whole artifact moved 500,000 rows by 48 MiB, and a fuller
projection made it *worse* — it bought a second read of the largest artifact. The
next front is a chunked decode, and it is named rather than attempted here.

## The idea the engine is built on

**A Kavo trace key is not destination match authority.** A synthetic key names a
delivered record so it can be traced to the source rows that produced it. It is
not evidence about anybody's CRM, and it never becomes a HubSpot unique property
or a Salesforce External ID. Matching requires a captured target contract, read
from the destination itself, and `UNKNOWN` never authorizes.

Two real instances found that guard open, twice:

- a HubSpot internal name is `kavo_trace_key`, and the comparison folded case
  only, so it walked straight past;
- the guard checked only the *running* adapter's spelling, so a HubSpot run
  naming the Salesforce trace key was accepted.

Both are closed, mutation-tested, and held by unit tests.

## What running against real instances corrected

Not one of these came from reading documentation.

**HubSpot.** The property export carries `Read only value` and `Calculated`, in
the file and in no documentation, and the parser read neither — so every property
reached the match authority with updateability `UNKNOWN`, which is refused, and
**UPSERT and UPDATE_ONLY against HubSpot were unreachable for every portal**. The
Imports API has no "Don't import column", so the trace-key column must be removed
before an API import and never mapped to a property. Associations therefore join
on the company's domain, the destination's own identity. And the portal refuses
`.example`, `.test`, `.invalid` and `.localhost` outright — which this
repository's own fixtures used throughout.

**Salesforce.** A describe that states the same picklist value twice is valid,
and the reader had been refusing real Salesforce data. Data Loader addresses a
parent by external id with a colon, not the dotted form the adapter documented.
`Opportunity.ContactId` exists, contrary to what the adapter said. And the org
answers in the running user's language, so a check asserting English error prose
passes only by luck.

## What this release does not claim

- That 1,000,000 rows fit the budget. They do not.
- That a property **Kavo creates** in a HubSpot portal behaves as one HubSpot
  ships. The qualification portal's credential carries no schema write scope, and
  the credential that does belongs to a live account holding real records, which
  no qualification may touch. Everything else about unique-property matching is
  established on `email`, which HubSpot itself reports unique.
- That the packages in `acceptance/` have been imported anywhere. They have not.
  The packages built from the qualification corpora have, into a real org and a
  real portal, and that is where the working claim comes from.
